system.name: PIPM
system.one_liner: a hardware-based partial and incremental page migration scheme for multi-host CXL disaggregated shared memory

flows.what: CXL/PCIe protocol messages over CXL Links

content.key_idea: Any number of hosts, each with local CPU/DRAM behind a CXL/PCIe root complex, attach over CXL Links to one shared CXL memory node for cache-coherent access.
content.reading_order: Left to right: the stacked host boxes, then the CXL Links arrow, then the CXL memory node on the right.

evidence: Figure 1 illustrates a multi-host CXL-DSM architecture comprising multiple compute nodes (hosts) connected to a CXL memory node.
By allowing multiple hosts to attach concurrently, CXL-DSM enables cache-coherent data sharing and collaborative computation across hosts.
The CXL controller manages connections and access to the attached memory.

summary: Figure 1 lays out the multi-host CXL-DSM background that PIPM builds on. One or more compute-node hosts (drawn as a stack of shadowed boxes to show that the count is arbitrary) each contain a CPU, a memory controller, local DRAM, and a CXL/PCIe root complex. Every host attaches over CXL Links to a single CXL disaggregated shared memory node, which mirrors the same internal structure: its own root complex, a CXL controller that manages access to the attached memory, a memory controller, and DRAM. The drawing is a plain, symmetric host-versus-device pair joined by one bold double-headed arrow standing in for the whole CXL link fabric; no coherence logic or data flow is shown yet, since this figure only establishes the hardware topology that later figures overlay with directories and PIPM's remapping tables.
